Research path

Four questions to ask when gold moves

Did real-rate expectations change?

Understand gold's opportunity cost and why the relationship can break.

Was the U.S. dollar involved?

Separate the dollar translation effect from other demand drivers.

Is structural demand changing?

Put central-bank purchases into a longer-term context.

Is this an inflation story?

Distinguish expected inflation, real yields and purchasing-power protection.

Frequently asked questions

Are these executable live prices?

No. Embedded data may be delayed and can differ from the price available through your broker, exchange or bullion dealer.

Does a technical “buy” label predict that gold will rise?

No. It summarizes selected indicators over a chosen interval. It is not a forecast, a probability or personalized advice.

Why focus on U.S. macro events?

Gold is commonly quoted in U.S. dollars. U.S. inflation, employment, growth and Federal Reserve events can change dollar and interest-rate expectations, although gold can respond differently from one event to the next.
